subject: Post-call: target price buckets + host comparisons for AcuityHealth
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mulligan <sarah@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: target price buckets + host comparisons for AcuityHealth

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the pricing benchmarking we ran in real time:

Summary (what we heard)
- Production use case: clinical summarization + triage assistant (high context lengths, frequent shorter completions and some long-form threads).
- Expected monthly usage: 150M–400M tokens (peak in month 3), with burst days up to ~25M tokens.
- Current procurement target: $/1M token guidance required for budget planning (procurement asked us to land a target before pilot).

Benchmark snapshot (illustrative $/1M, Jan 2026):
- OpenAI (gpt-4o/production variant): ~$1,200–1,600 per 1M tokens (hosted, includes context + generation)
- Anthropic (Claude Pro): ~$900–1,300 per 1M
- Major open-model hosts (NGC/HostX): $450–800 per 1M depending on quantization and committed tiers
- Redwood inference (pilot guidance): we can target $/1M between $400–700 depending on committed volume, batching, and caching profile; dedicated reserved pools drive the lower end.

Key asks for us to firm an offer
1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens (best estimate between 3–12 months).
2) Desired target $/1M (procurement suggested a target band — if you can share the exact budgeted $/1M that helps us finalize the pilot SOW).
3) Any compliance evidence/time constraints (SOC2 report, regional data residency) that would affect private deployment pricing.

Attachments: I attached a compact benchmark workbook (redwood-benchmarks-1m-breakdown.xlsx) that models unit economics under 3 configs (hosted, reserved/dedicated, private).

Next steps
- If you can reply with a preferred $/1M target band and a best-guess monthly token number by EOD Thu, we’ll produce a pilot pricing proposal (including a 30-day commitment option + optional reserved tier pricing) and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks — looping Ben and Laura for input on recommended offer structure.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Sarah Mulligan <sarah@acuityhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acuityhealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: target price buckets + host comparisons for AcuityHealth

Markus — thanks for the summary and workbook. A few clarifications from procurement and product:

1) We can confirm a starting pilot expected at ~60M tokens/month (month 1–2) ramping to ~220M/month by month 6. Peak days could hit 20–30M.
2) Procurement asked if we can get to a target of $500 per 1M tokens for the pilot, with a roadmap to $375–$450/1M once we hit committed reserved capacity (6–12 month commit).
3) Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required for production; initial pilot can run in your hosted region (US) under a data processing addendum. If Private/VPC is necessary we’ll flag it in month 3.

We’re comfortable with a short pilot commitment (30 days) if we can lock a price band and visibility into how you plan to get to the reserved-tier numbers. Can you also indicate the expected latency regime for the long-context flows (1–2s 95p target for summarization)?

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if easier.

—Sarah
Sarah Mulligan
Head of Product, AcuityHealth
sarah@acuityhealth.com

On Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 3:20 PM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery...

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Post-call: target price buckets + host comparisons for AcuityHealth

Ben/Laura — Sarah confirmed the numbers (quoted below). Procurement wants a pilot target at $500/1M with a path to $375–$450 at reserve. They also want SOC2 for production and a 30-day pilot.

My suggested approach for an offer (short and actionable):
- Pilot price (30 days, no long-term commit): $495/1M (hosted) — includes typical prefix caching and 10% introductory credit to cover variance.
- Reserved pilot option (3 months reserve, rollback to reserved pool if we exceed thresholds): $420/1M with 6-month ramp clauses to $375 at 220M+ tokens/month.
- Latency commitment for summarization flows: target 95th percentile <= 2s on Dedicated pools (we’ll include benchmark traces and SLA language in the pilot SOW).

Why this structure?
- Aligns to their procurement target (500) while preserving the ability to price down for committed volume.
- Gives Acuity a clear pathway to reserved economics we benchmarked vs other hosts (open-hosts as low as $450/1M but require aggressive quantization and dedicated infra).

Ask: Ben — can you build a short pricing one-pager showing the two lanes (Pilot: $495/1M hosted; Reserved: $420->$375/1M) plus the assumptions (avg tokens per req, batching, expected cache hit)? Put it in the MAP draft (linked) and I’ll send to Sarah with the pilot SOW.

Thanks — Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: target price buckets + host comparisons for AcuityHealth

Sarah — thanks for the quick confirm and the target band. We’ll do the following:

1) Formal pilot proposal by EOD Mon: 30-day hosted pilot at $495/1M tokens. Includes 10% buffer credit, standard DPA (US region), SOC2 evidence links.
2) MAP + reserved pricing appendix: draft reserved option at $420/1M with ramp to $375/1M at 220M+ tokens/month.
3) Metrics pack: expected latency summary (95p <= 2s on dedicated; hosted target 95p ~ 2.5s depending on queueing) and sample benchmark traces.

If that sounds good I’ll attach the pilot SOW and a short pricing one-pager (Ben will add the assumptions). Then we can route to procurement for approval and a quick signature.

Next steps: Sarah — can you share the procurement contact for signatures (name/email) and confirm whether the pilot needs to be under your standard PO or via a short contract?

Best regards,
Markus Klein
